The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in short, is that the present petitioner as plaintiff filed the above numbered suit against the defendant-opposite parties being No. 1321 of 2008 before the learned District Judge, Khulna as part of the central filing system, prevailing at the relevant time though the suit was triable by the Assistant Judge, for declaration that the judgment dated 30-9-1958 and the decree dated 6·11·1958 in Title Suit No. 160 of 1957 passed by the then Subordinate Judge, Khulna is void, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 6. After filing of the suit the petitioner filed an application In the trial Court on 27·1·2009 under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying the operation of the Judgment and decree dated 30-9-1958 and 6-11-1958 of the Title suit No. 160 of 1957. But the trial Court was pleased to reject the said application by his order dated 18-11-2009. 

 10. 'On the other hand, Dr. Naim Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No.1 opposes the Rule. He submits that Indra Sekhar Chakraborti, the predecessor of the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff filed the impugned title Suit being No. 160 of 1957 for declaration of title and permanent injunction into 4 bighas of land fully described in the schedule of that suit and in the said suit the then Province of East Pakistan was the defendant No. 1 and District Board, Khulna was defendant No.2 and the suit was decreed on contest by a judgment dated 30-9- 1958. Against the said judgment, the Government of the then East Pakistan preferred an Appeal being Title Appeal No. 57 of 1959 before the High Court and the High Court ultimately by its judgment dated 12-12-1978 affirmed the judgment of the trial Court. The opposite party No. 1 being the legal heirs of the said Indra Sekhar Chakrabarti while was in possession of the suit land all on a sudden on 2-8-2005 the present petitioner, that is the Khulna Zilla Parishad had entered into the suit land forcibly and started making semi pucca construction and under the said compelling circumstances the opposite party No. 1 filed Execution Proceeding No.5 of 2007 before the Joint district Judge, 1st Court, Khulna under Order XXI Rule 32 and section 151 of the CPC. He submits that though the District Board, Khulna, that is, the defendant No.2 of that suit did not contes.t in the suit but the Government of the then East Pakistan contested the suit. So, the interest of the defendant No.2 has been rightly protected by the defendant No.1. So, the defendant No.2 at this stage cannot file a suit taking the ground of fraud, collusiveness or any other grounds and the suit was filed after almost 50 years of the decree with a malafide intention to cause harm to the opposite party No .I and both the Courts below being convinced of the said fact did not stay the operation of the judgment and decree of the former suit dated 30-9-1958 which was affirmed by the High Court even. So, the Courts below particularly the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Khulna on due consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case did not commit any error of law by his impugned order occasioning failure of justice to the petitioner. So, the Rule is liable to be discharged with costs,
